Kapampangan

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • bebai (obsolete)

Etymology

[edit]

From earlier bebai, from Proto-Philippine *baybay. Compare Tagalog baybay.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbebe/ [ˈbɛː.bɛː]
  • Hyphenation: be‧be

Noun

[edit]

bébé

  1. seashore
  2. riverbank
  3. mountainside

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bebebe
  • binebayan
  • binebe
  • mabebe
  • Macabebe
  • makabebe
  • minebe

Makasar

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbebe/, [ˈɓɛ.bɛ]
  • Hyphenation: be‧be

Noun

[edit]

bebe (Lontara spelling ᨅᨙᨅᨙ)

  1. drool

Synonyms

[edit]
  • piʼru (saliva)
  • iloroʼ (moisture in the mouth)

Affixations

[edit]
  • aʼbebe
  • bebèi

Further reading

[edit]
  • A. A. Cense (2024), Makassaars-Nederlands woordenboek‎[2], Brill, →DOI

Romanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bébé and also influenced by English baby.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbe.be/, /beˈbe/

Noun

[edit]

bebe m (uncountable)

  1. baby, infant
    Synonyms: bebeluș, copilaș

vocative bebe

bebe

Sranan Tongo

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Probably from Fon gbɛ̀gbɛ́-tín (“Pterocarpus tree”).[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bebe/, [bɪ̞bɪ̞], [be̝be̝]

Noun

[edit]

bebe

  1. any tree of the genus Pterocarpus

Derived terms

[edit]
  • basrabebe
  • bergibebe
  • dyukabebe
  • heigronbebe
  • manbebe
  • watrabebe

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Norval Smith (2009), “A preliminary list of probable Gbe lexical items in the Surinam Creoles”, in P. Muysken, N. Smith, editors, Surviving the Middle Passage: The West Africa-Surinam Sprachbund, Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton, →ISBN, page 468.

West Makian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Reduplication of be (“water”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /be.ˈbe/

Verb

[edit]

bebe

  1. (transitive, informal) to drink
    Synonym: joube (polite)

Conjugation

[edit]
Conjugation of bebe (action verb)
singular plural
inclusive exclusive
1st person tebebe mebebe abebe
2nd person nebebe febebe
3rd person inanimate ibebe debebe
animate
imperative nebebe, bebe febebe, bebe

References

[edit]
  • Clemens Voorhoeve (1982), The Makian languages and their neighbours‎[3], Pacific linguistics (as bebé)
